result.method_note:
All work read-only in /home/user/superbot @ 5e3a667b. Commands run verbatim:
(1) `cat disbot/core/runtime/navigation_stack.py`, `panel_manifest.py`, `persistent_views.py`; `cat disbot/views/navigation.py`, `disbot/views/base.py`, `disbot/views/hub_children.py`, `disbot/cogs/help/route.py`, `disbot/cogs/help/panels.py`, `disbot/cogs/help_cog.py`, `disbot/utils/hub_registry.py`, `disbot/views/games/hub.py`, `disbot/views/moderation/main_panel.py`, `disbot/views/server_management/hub.py`.
(2) Registry parsed with python3 `ast` (not regex): SUBSYSTEMS from disbot/utils/subsystem_registry.py -> 43 entries, 34 with parent_hub, 9 without; HUBS from disbot/utils/hub_registry.py -> 8 entries. Bidirectional roster diff hub.primary_children vs the parent_hub filter -> 0 drift in both directions on all 8 hubs.
(3) `discord` and `asyncpg` are NOT installed in this container, so tools/sim/help_menu_grouping_sim.py could not be imported directly. I REIMPLEMENTED its click model verbatim from source (help_menu_grouping_sim.py:126-215: PAGE_SIZE=12, TIER_RANK, LEAVES=SUBSYSTEMS-{"help"}, section_of, visible_children, clicks_to) over the AST-parsed registries. Result: 42 leaves, 8 sections, admin tier -> 8 leaves at 1 click, 34 at 2 clicks, max=2, 0 orphans, largest section=10 (< PAGE_SIZE). user tier -> 25 visible, 6 at 1 click, 19 at 2. moderator -> 27 visible, all <= 2.
(4) `python3 scripts/check_consistency.py --mode strict > out 2>&1; echo $?` -> REAL_EXIT=0, "check_consistency: all rules passed".
(5) Built minimal stub `discord`/`discord.ext.commands`/`asyncpg`/`dotenv` modules in scratchpad, then `PYTHONPATH=<stub> python3 scripts/check_command_reachability.py --json > out 2>&1; echo $?` -> REAL_EXIT=0, {"reachable": 95, "exempt": 147, "gaps": []}. Re-ran its own classification loop with instrumentation: {'operator_or_owner_tier': 87, 'reachable': 95, 'hidden': 56, 'help_root': 1, 'allowlisted': 3}, TOTAL 242.
(6) View census via ast over disbot/{views,cogs,core,services,utils} with transitive base resolution: 282 view classes; 54 with an effective SUBSYSTEM (declared or inherited); 51 of those with STANDARD_NAV on; 51 classes extending discord.ui.View directly.
(7) Consumer counts by grep with real exit codes captured to files (no `cmd | head; $?`): attach_back_button -> 41 call sites in 34 distinct files outside views/navigation.py; discover_hub_children -> 3 hub consumers; HubChildButton -> 3 subclasses; navigation_stack.{push,pop,current,root,depth} -> 0 non-test callers; `_PAGE_SIZE` -> 0 occurrences anywhere under disbot/; "leaderboard" in disbot/views/economy/main_panel.py -> grep -c returned 0.
Did NOT run pytest (no discord/asyncpg), so every test-derived row below is classed TEST-PROVEN from reading the test, never from a green run.

strengths.claim: The universal Help + Back-to-hub controls are attached inside TWO base-class constructors (views.base.BaseView.__init__ and core.runtime.persistent_views.PersistentView.__init__), not by per-view code, so they survive the edit_in_place redraw idiom that drops externally-attached buttons. I counted 51 view classes (of 282 total view classes) that carry an effective SUBSYSTEM with STANDARD_NAV left on and therefore receive it automatically.
strengths.prevents_failure: panel-redraw back-loss: a panel that redraws onto a fresh view instance loses the Back/Help button its parent attached to the original instance, stranding the user (named in source as 'the games/admin panel back-loss class')
strengths.successor_recommendation: Keep 'nav is attached by the base constructor, not by each panel' as a hard rule in the rebuild. It is the single mechanism that makes the 2-tap claim survive redraws, and it costs one line per base class.

strengths.claim: Help reachability is enforced by a CI invariant that is itself mutation-tested. tests/unit/invariants/test_help_reachability.py asserts check_reachability() == [] AND has a second test that deliberately removes 'blackjack' from the live scheme and asserts the orphan detector flags exactly it. pytest runs on every code change in .github/workflows/code-quality.yml:267-279 (`pytest tests/ -v -n auto --tb=short`).
strengths.quote:
def test_guard_has_teeth_detects_an_unhomed_subsystem(sim):
    """The guard must actually catch an orphan — a vacuous check is worse than
    none. Simulate a regression by dropping a known child from its section and
    confirm the orphan detector flags exactly it.
    """
strengths.prevents_failure: silent orphaning: a subsystem added or re-parented without a route into !help becomes completely unreachable from the menu, because the catch-all 'All Commands / Advanced' browser was removed in PR #1294 and there is no fallback surface
strengths.successor_recommendation: Rebuild MUST carry a reachability invariant with a teeth test. The teeth test is the reason this one is worth anything — copy that shape, not just the assertion.

strengths.claim: The route table is bidirectionally consistent with zero drift, measured by AST: 8 hubs, 34 children, and for every hub the set(primary_children) and the set of SUBSYSTEMS with parent_hub==hub.key are identical in BOTH directions (0 keys only-in-hub, 0 keys only-in-registry on all 8). 43 subsystems = 8 hub hosts + 34 children + help itself, so no subsystem is un-homed.
strengths.quote:
Two implicit contracts bite when you edit this:
            (1) **bidirectional roster rule** — every key here MUST set
            ``parent_hub=<key>`` in ``SUBSYSTEMS`` and vice versa, or
            ``services/help_catalogue.py`` reports ``roster_drift`` and
            ``test_every_hub_primary_children_match_parent_hub_filter``
            fails;
strengths.prevents_failure: roster drift: a hub advertising a child the registry does not home (or vice versa), which makes a subsystem appear in one surface and vanish from another
strengths.successor_recommendation: Keep exactly one direction of truth instead. Superbot needs a bidirectional-consistency checker only because it stores the parent link twice (hub.primary_children AND subsystem.parent_hub). The rebuild should store it once and derive the other.

strengths.claim: Route-table depth measured, not estimated: reimplementing clicks_to() from tools/sim/help_menu_grouping_sim.py:197-215 over the live registries gives, at administrator tier, 8 subsystems at 1 click and 34 at 2 clicks — max 2, mean 1.81, 0 orphans, largest section 10 children (under PAGE_SIZE=12). At user tier 25 of 42 leaves are visible and all 25 are <= 2 clicks; at moderator tier 27 of 42, all <= 2. The estate's '2 taps' claim is TRUE of the route table.
strengths.quote: MAX_CLICKS = 3  # the reachability contract: every feature reachable in <= 3 clicks
strengths.prevents_failure: deep menus: a feature buried more than 2 picks from !help, or a hub whose child list paginates and silently adds a click
strengths.successor_recommendation: Adopt the contract (max depth as a numeric CI assertion) but see P1-D2: this measures the ROUTE TABLE, not the rendered panels. The rebuild's depth check must walk the actual components.

strengths.claim: The 'a navigable panel must offer a way back' rule is a graduated ERROR-severity AST rule wired into CI, not a convention. I ran it: `python3 scripts/check_consistency.py --mode strict` exits 0 with 'all rules passed' at HEAD 5e3a667b. It has 14 scoped allowlist entries in architecture_rules/consistency_exceptions.yml, each with a written reason, and the allowlist header forbids allowlisting a genuine child gap.
strengths.quote:
Rule(
        "back_button",
        rule_back_button,
        "HubView navigation panels with child controls but no back/nav affordance",
        severity="error",
    ),
strengths.prevents_failure: dead-end panel: a child sub-panel with child controls and no back affordance anywhere in its module (the Explore world-hub dead-end that shipped before the rule was widened to add_item-built hubs)
strengths.successor_recommendation: The graduation discipline is the transferable part: warn-only until the tree is clean, then flip severity to error and wire into CI, with a per-class allowlist that carries a reason string. Copy that, not the specific AST heuristics.

strengths.claim: The command-level guard runs clean and its baseline is empty. I ran `scripts/check_command_reachability.py --json` (with stubbed discord/asyncpg/dotenv): 242 prefix commands, 95 reachable, 147 exempt, 0 gaps. Instrumenting its own loop gives the exempt breakdown: 87 operator/owner-tier, 56 Discord-hidden, 1 help root, 3 allowlisted. So the guarded surface is 95 of 242 commands, and all 95 pass.
strengths.quote:
It drives ``scripts/check_command_reachability.py`` (the static checker) and
**ratchets against a recorded baseline** (Q-0105 warn-first): the pre-existing
orphan-cog gaps are tolerated, but any *new* unreachable member command fails —
which is what makes "every command findable" un-regressable while the per-cog
audit follow-on sessions clear the baseline.
strengths.prevents_failure: unfindable cog: a member-tier command whose cog maps to no homed+discoverable subsystem, so it never appears in any help listing (the owner-reported 'the general cog is completely unfindable from the help menu')
strengths.successor_recommendation: Steal the shrink-only baseline mechanism (test_baseline_has_no_stale_entries fails when a listed gap is fixed but not removed) — it is how superbot got from 'many gaps' to zero without a big-bang. But note the guard proves LISTING reachability, not BUTTON reachability.

strengths.claim: The Games-hub contract does not check button shape statically — it invokes each button's real callback against a stubbed Interaction and classifies by which response method was awaited (send_modal / send_message / edit_message with a different view), then asserts at least one button classifies action_*. A separate coverage gate asserts the strict target list EQUALS the set of visible parent_hub=='games' subsystems, so a new game cannot be added without being forced into the list. 8 strict targets + 2 strict-xfail (fishing, creature) = all 10 Games children covered.
strengths.quote:
registry_games = _games_subsystems_from_registry()
    # M1 of the BTD6-top-level + AI-central-policy initiative
    # promoted BTD6 to its own top-level hub; it is no longer a
    # Games child. The actionability contract for BTD6 lives in
    # the BTD6 cog's own tests now.
strengths.prevents_failure: instruction-only dead end: a hub child whose panel only swaps in a 'type !command' embed or an empty discord.ui.View, so clicking through Help reaches no action
strengths.successor_recommendation: This is the single strongest navigation artifact in the repo and the one to generalise: it is the only guard that proves a BUTTON DOES SOMETHING rather than that a route exists. Extend its scope from the Games hub to every hub in the rebuild; today 10 of 34 children are covered.

strengths.claim: One resolver, three entry points. cogs/help/route.py::resolve_route is called by the `!help <name>` prefix command (help_cog.py:302), the `/help name:` slash command (help_cog.py:406) and the Help dropdown callback (cogs/help/panels.py:110), so a typed name and a clicked option cannot resolve to different destinations. open_route additionally checks every destination against the audience HelpProjection so a governance-hidden target renders the same not-found embed as a nonexistent name.
strengths.quote:
The resolver is the only place Help routing logic lives. Both the
    typed ``!help <name>`` command and the Help dropdown call this so the
    same name produces the same destination regardless of entry point.
strengths.prevents_failure: surface divergence: typed help and clicked help disagreeing about what exists, and information leak where a hidden surface is typed-reachable but not advertised
strengths.successor_recommendation: Non-negotiable for the rebuild: one resolver shared by every front door (prefix, slash, component), and the audience projection applied INSIDE the opener rather than at each call site.

strengths.claim: Child discovery and child-forwarding are one seam with three consumers each: discover_hub_children is called from views/games/hub.py:97, views/community/hub.py and cogs/utility_cog.py:42, and HubChildButton has exactly three thin subclasses (_GameHubButton, _CommunityChildButton, _UtilityChildButton). The module's own docstring records the failure it replaced: three hand-rolled copies, one of which rendered none of the Utility panel's children.
strengths.quote:
A *mother hub* (Games, Community, Utility, …) surfaces the subsystems that
declare ``parent_hub == <hub key>`` as child buttons on its panel.  Before this
module each hub re-implemented the same "filter ``SUBSYSTEMS`` by ``parent_hub``,
sort deterministically" discovery by hand (``views.games.hub.discover_game_children``,
``views.community.hub.discover_community_children``,
``cogs.utility_cog.discover_utility_children``).  Three copies meant a hub could
silently drift — the exact class behind the *discoverability audit* general-cog
bug, where the Utility panel rendered none of its children.
strengths.prevents_failure: hub discovery drift: a hub whose hand-written child list falls behind the registry, rendering fewer children than are homed under it
strengths.simpler_than_counterpart: The three hand-rolled discover_*_children copies it replaced.
strengths.successor_recommendation: Make registry-driven child rendering the ONLY way a hub panel gets its children in the rebuild. Superbot's residual damage (P1-D1, P1-D7) is entirely in the 5 hubs that never adopted this seam.

defects.claim: The Moderation & Safety hub panel renders ZERO of its 6 registry children as buttons. ModPanelView has exactly 7 decorated buttons (Warn/Timeout/Kick/Ban/Unban/Mod Logs/Clear Warnings), no add_item call and no select. Grepping the whole tree for a button that opens automod, image_moderation, proof_channel or security returns nothing — 4 of 34 hub children have no child-opening button anywhere in disbot/. cleanup and logging have a button only on the Server & Admin panel (administrator tier), not on their declared parent hub. Counting all button paths: 30 of 34 children are button-reachable at administrator tier, 27 of 34 from their own declared parent hub, and 4 of 34 from nowhere.
defects.failure_scenario: A guild administrator types !help, picks 'Moderation & Safety' from the dropdown, and sees the mod dashboard with seven action buttons. Automod, Image Moderation, Proof Channel and Security are all homed under this hub in the registry and all four cogs implement build_help_menu_view, but no button on this panel (or any other panel) opens them. The admin must already know to type !automod / !imagemod / !security / !prizemenu. The claim 'the only command anyone ever needs is !help, from there you can use every feature' is false for these four features.
defects.successor_recommendation: In the rebuild, a hub panel MUST render its children from the registry (the HubChildButton seam) rather than hand-written buttons. Five of superbot's eight hubs render children by hand and that is where 100% of the button gaps are.

defects.claim: The CI reachability invariant is computed from the REGISTRY, never from the rendered panels, so it is green while P1-D1 holds. clicks_to() resolves a leaf's section from Scheme metadata built out of hub.primary_children / parent_hub; it never instantiates a view or inspects a component. My reimplementation of it reports automod, image_moderation, proof_channel and security at exactly 2 clicks — the same 2 the guard accepts — while no button exists to make either click. This is not hypothetical: the same class already shipped once, with treasury.
defects.quote:
section = scheme.section_of(leaf)
    if section is not None:
        # The section host itself is reached by one index pick.
        if leaf == section.key:
            return 1
        # A child: index pick + dropdown pick, +1 per extra dropdown page.
        kids = visible_children(section, tier)
defects.failure_scenario: A maintainer adds a subsystem, sets parent_hub on it, adds it to the hub's primary_children, and ships. Every guard goes green: test_help_reachability passes (registry says 2 clicks), test_discoverability passes (the cog has build_help_menu_view), check_command_reachability reports 0 gaps (the subsystem is homed and discoverable), check_consistency passes (no HubView lost a back button). A user then opens !help, picks the hub, and finds no button for the new feature. This is exactly what happened to treasury: 'the Economy hub panel hardcodes its buttons ... so treasury had no clickable entry — reachable only by typing !treasury / !help treasury' (tests/unit/views/test_economy_treasury_button.py:4-8).
defects.successor_recommendation: The rebuild's reachability check must walk the CONSTRUCTED components (build each hub panel, read its children's custom_ids, assert every registry child appears) — the actionability contract already proves this is affordable: it instantiates cogs and invokes callbacks in-process. Registry-only reachability is the load-bearing lie in superbot's navigation story.

defects.claim: core/runtime/navigation_stack.py — the 151-line 'per-session breadcrumb navigation stack' with a documented public surface of push/pop/current/root/depth/forget, per-session asyncio locks, DB persistence and a diagnostics provider — has ZERO production callers for its navigation half. Grepping disbot/ and tests/ for navigation_stack.{push,pop,current,root,depth} returns 18 hits, all 18 in tests/unit/runtime/test_navigation_stack.py. Every non-test import (guild_lifecycle.py:241, session_gc.py:53, session_manager.py:90/114) calls only forget(), the lock-cleanup function. Real navigation is closure-based (BackTarget/chain_back), which views/navigation.py:126-128 describes as unwinding 'without inventing a router or a stack'.
defects.quote:
Public surface:
    push(session_id, screen_id, data)  → None
    pop(session_id)                    → ScreenState | None
    current(session_id)                → ScreenState | None  (read-only)
    root(session_id)                   → None  (clear stack)
    depth(session_id)                  → int  (read-only)
    forget(session_id)                 → None (drop the lock)
defects.failure_scenario: A rebuild session reads the estate record 'navigation works via a navigation stack', ports navigation_stack.py first, and builds the new bot's Back handling on push/pop — reproducing 151 lines of DB-backed, lock-guarded state that superbot's live navigation has never once called. The real mechanism it needs to port is the 41 attach_back_button call sites across 34 files plus BackTarget/chain_back/carry_back.
defects.successor_recommendation: Do not port navigation_stack.py. Decide deliberately between a real stack and closure-chaining; superbot chose closures and never removed the stack, so the file is a trap for anyone reading the tree to learn how navigation works.

defects.claim: No artifact in superbot binds a button to a command, so the claim 'every command is reachable and ACTIVATED BY a button' is unverifiable from source by construction. The panel manifest — the one typed, runtime-built projection of every persistent panel's real components — declares the field and permanently leaves it None because no such binding is declared anywhere. Consequently the two reachability guards prove different, weaker things: check_command_reachability proves a command's COG is help-discoverable (95 of 242 commands, 87 exempted as operator/owner-tier and 56 as Discord-hidden), and test_help_reachability proves a SUBSYSTEM is homed. Neither touches commands-per-button.
defects.quote:
``action_id`` is the logical action id; ``custom_id`` is the Discord
    component id. They are identical today (custom_ids are fully static) — the
    field is kept distinct so a future dynamic-suffix custom_id can still expose
    a stable logical action. ``command`` (which command this action invokes) is
    deferred: there is no declared button→command binding yet, and the manifest
    spine exists to eliminate *unverified* metadata, so it stays ``None`` rather
    than be guessed.
defects.failure_scenario: The rebuild plan inherits 'every command is activated by a button' as a settled property and writes it into the new bot's acceptance criteria. Nothing in superbot can be pointed at to define, count or regression-test it: no manifest field is populated, no test asserts it, and the panel manifest's own author refused to guess it. The first honest attempt to verify the claim in the new bot has to invent the binding from scratch.
defects.successor_recommendation: Declare the button->command binding at the source of the button in the rebuild (e.g. every panel button names the command or capability it invokes), so the manifest can populate it and a single test can assert 'every non-hidden member-tier command is named by at least one reachable button'. That test does not exist anywhere in superbot and is the only thing that would make the headline claim checkable.

defects.claim: attach_standard_nav's opt-out test is a substring match on button LABELS, so a panel whose buttons merely mention 'help' silently loses the universal Help control. ServerManagementHubView (PersistentView, SUBSYSTEM='server_management', parent_hub='admin') declares buttons labelled '👁 Help Preview' and '✏️ Help editor'; _self_navigates() matches 'help' in those labels, returns True, and attach_standard_nav returns before attaching either the 📚 Help button or the ↩ Server & Admin button. 1 of the 51 auto-nav-eligible view classes is suppressed this way. The source itself flags the risk: 'Heuristic — if a future panel's button copy diverges this may misfire'.
defects.quote:
label = (getattr(child, "label", None) or "").lower()
        # "overview" is deliberately absent — it is a self-refresh, not
        # parent-nav (the LoggingPanelView / EconomyPanelView stranding class).
        if "help" in label or "back to" in label:
            return True
    return False
defects.failure_scenario: An administrator runs !help, picks 'Server & Admin', clicks '🧭 Server Management'. The panel that opens has no 📚 Help button — the contract promises every SUBSYSTEM panel is one click from Help. The user sees '👁 Help Preview' and clicks it expecting to get back to the menu, and instead lands in the guild Help-overlay preview. Returning to Help actually takes two clicks (↩ Back to Admin, then 📚 Help), and only because admin_cog._open_via_help_hook happens to attach a back-to-Admin button externally; a panel opened by any route that does not do that would be stranded outright.
defects.successor_recommendation: Never decide navigation structure from user-facing copy. In the rebuild, a panel opts out of standard nav with an explicit flag (superbot already has STANDARD_NAV=False, used by only 6 classes) or by carrying a nav-typed component, never by label text.

defects.claim: The reachability guard enforces a dropdown-pagination cap against a surface that no longer exists, and therefore cannot see the cap that is actually live. help_menu_grouping_sim.py:63 sets PAGE_SIZE=12 'mirrors cogs/help/panels.py `_PAGE_SIZE`' — grepping disbot/ for `_PAGE_SIZE` returns 0 occurrences (the paginated Advanced browser was removed in PR #1294; cogs/help/panels.py is 143 lines and has no pagination). Hub children are rendered as BUTTONS, capped by Discord at 5 per row / 25 per view. Two of the three registry-driven hubs wrap rows (games/hub.py:349-364, community/hub.py:288-308); the third pins every child to a single hardcoded row.
defects.quote:
# Surface child subsystems as forwarding buttons (row 3 — rows 0-2 hold the
        # cog's own actions, row 4 is reserved for the help layer's Back button).
        # Rendered unfiltered; visibility is enforced at click time in
        # _UtilityChildButton.callback (matches the Community hub's unfiltered path).
        for subsystem, meta in discover_utility_children():
            self.add_item(
                _UtilityChildButton(
                    subsystem=subsystem,
                    label=_format_child_label(subsystem, meta),
                    row=3,
                ),
            )
defects.failure_scenario: A maintainer adds a sixth subsystem with parent_hub='utility' (there are 2 today). Every guard passes: the sim's cap is 12 and 6 < 12. At runtime _UtilityPanelView.__init__ calls add_item for the sixth button on row 3, discord.py raises ValueError because a row holds at most 5 components (views/navigation.py:266-276 catches exactly this for its own button and logs a warning; this call site is unguarded), build_help_menu_view raises, and cogs/help/route.py::open_route's hub branch catches it and returns build_not_found_embed(hub.display_name) with view=None. A user who picks 'Utility' from the Help dropdown gets an ephemeral reading 'No command or category named Utility found.' — the whole Utility section disappears from Help.
defects.successor_recommendation: Cap enforcement must live where the components are built, not in a simulation of a removed surface. In the rebuild, hub child layout goes through one packer that wraps rows and asserts the 25-component ceiling, and the depth guard reads the packer's output.

defects.claim: The Economy hub panel does not render one of its three declared primary_children. `grep -c leaderboard disbot/views/economy/main_panel.py` returns 0, while hub_registry.py:155-165 lists leaderboard among economy's primary_children. Its 8 economy: buttons are daily/work/shop/balance/inventory/jobs/treasury/overview. Leaderboard is button-reachable only because the Community hub renders it as a cross-link (hub_registry.py:209-213 + community/hub.py:301-308) — i.e. under a different hub than the one that owns it.
defects.failure_scenario: A member types !help, picks 'Economy' expecting the standings feature the hub's own purpose line advertises ('Currency, items, work, shop, and standings'), and finds no Leaderboard button on the Economy panel. They reach it only by guessing the Community hub instead, or by typing !leaderboard / !lb. Nothing in CI reports this because the registry says leaderboard is homed under economy and the guard only reads the registry (P1-D2).
defects.successor_recommendation: Same fix as P1-D1/P1-D2: registry-driven child rendering plus a rendered-panel reachability assertion. This row and the treasury regression are the same defect firing twice on the same hand-written panel.

honest_nulls: I could NOT run superbot's test suite. `discord` and `asyncpg` are not installed in this container and I was told not to install anything. Every test-derived claim above (test_help_reachability, test_help_actionability_contract, test_command_reachability, test_navigation) is from READING the test, not from observing it pass. I did run the two standalone scripts (check_consistency.py: real exit 0; check_command_reachability.py under stub modules: real exit 0), and I reimplemented the sim's click model rather than importing it.

I could NOT verify that superbot's `code-quality` workflow is a REQUIRED status check on main. I read the workflow file (it runs check_consistency --mode strict at line 211 and pytest at line 279 on code changes) but did not query the branch-protection/rulesets API for menno420/superbot. So 'ci_check' above means 'runs in the CI workflow', not 'blocks merge'.

I could NOT establish button-level reachability for the ~228 view classes that are neither hubs nor SUBSYSTEM-declaring panels (282 view classes total, 54 with an effective SUBSYSTEM). My reachability numbers are at the SUBSYSTEM/PANEL level. Whether every leaf sub-view inside e.g. the AI, settings or channels panels can be reached and exited by button is unmeasured here.

The 30-of-34 button-reachability figure counts a button EXISTING that names the child subsystem; I did not execute any hub panel's constructor (no discord), so I did not verify that all 30 buttons actually render under governance filtering at a given tier. The 4-of-34 zero-button figure is stronger: it is the absence of any such call site in the whole tree.

I did NOT test the tier-visibility interaction the sim's clicks_to() ignores. clicks_to checks only tier_of(leaf) > tier and never checks whether the leaf's SECTION is visible to that tier. I checked for the case it would break on (a leaf visible to a tier whose hub is not) and found zero instances today across user/moderator/administrator — so the omission is currently latent, not firing, and I have no evidence about whether it ever fired.

Several tests in tests/unit/views/test_navigation.py (44 tests) assert on SOURCE TEXT rather than behaviour — e.g. `assert "attach_back_button" in src`, `assert "HelpCategoryView" in src`. I counted 4 such greps but did not audit all 44, so I cannot state what fraction of that file's coverage is behavioural.

I did not read docs/help-command-surface-map.md itself, only its guard (tests/unit/docs/test_help_surface_map_doc.py), which checks that the doc exists, has the expected headings, and mentions every subsystem and hub by name. I therefore cannot say whether the doc's PROSE is accurate — only that its inventory is name-complete.

On question 5 (help corpus generation): the rendered help text IS generated, not authored — build_cog_embed walks live cog.get_commands() and reads cmd.help docstrings, build_categories_overview_embed reads HUBS via the projection, hub panels read SUBSYSTEMS. I found no hand-authored help-copy data file (searched disbot/**/*.{json,yml,yaml} and for help_text/HELP_TEXT/help_entries). What is separately maintained is (a) the guild-level DB overlay for rename/hide/re-describe (services/help_overlay, display-only) and (b) the docs/help-command-surface-map.md inventory. I did not measure whether any cog's docstrings have drifted from behaviour — that is a content question no guard in this repo asks.

result.lane: P2 — superbot navigation reachability from the user-journey side
result.method_note:
All reads in /home/user/superbot @ 5e3a667b, read-only, nothing run against a live bot (discord.py is not installed here — `python3 scripts/check_command_reachability.py` fails with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'discord', so every "gap count" below is from source, never from executing a checker).

Files opened in full or in cited ranges: disbot/cogs/help/panels.py, disbot/cogs/help/route.py, disbot/cogs/help_cog.py, disbot/views/help/home_builder.py, disbot/views/navigation.py, disbot/views/hub_children.py, disbot/views/base.py, disbot/core/runtime/persistent_views.py, disbot/services/help_projection.py, disbot/governance/resolver.py, disbot/utils/hub_registry.py, disbot/utils/subsystem_registry.py, disbot/cogs/quicksetup_cog.py, disbot/cogs/setup_cog.py, disbot/cogs/setup/_wizard_entry.py, disbot/views/setup/launcher.py, disbot/views/setup/essential_setup.py, disbot/cogs/role_cog.py, disbot/views/roles/role_menu_view.py, disbot/views/roles/reaction_panel.py, disbot/views/roles/role_menu_builder.py, disbot/services/reaction_role_service.py, disbot/utils/role_feasibility.py, disbot/cogs/settings_cog.py, disbot/views/settings/hub.py, disbot/views/settings/subsystem_view.py, disbot/views/settings/edit_boolean.py, disbot/views/settings/edit_command_access.py, disbot/cogs/ticket_cog.py, disbot/views/tickets/{hub,launcher,_shared}.py, disbot/services/ticket_service.py, disbot/services/ticket_mutation.py, disbot/cogs/bootstrap_access_cog.py, disbot/core/runtime/command_access.py, disbot/cogs/admin_cog.py, disbot/views/moderation/main_panel.py, disbot/views/community/hub.py, disbot/cogs/community_cog.py, disbot/bot1.py, scripts/check_consistency.py, scripts/check_command_reachability.py, tools/sim/help_menu_grouping_sim.py, tests/unit/invariants/{test_help_reachability,test_command_reachability,test_bootstrap_access_load_order}.py, .github/workflows/code-quality.yml.

Counting commands actually run (verbatim):
- `grep -rn "^    SUBSYSTEM\s*[:=]" disbot/views disbot/cogs --include=*.py | grep -v '= ""' | wc -l` → 54 lines, of which 53 are real values (one is `SUBSYSTEM = SUBSYSTEM`); a python/ast cross-check against subsystem_registry keys returned `[]` unknown values.
- `grep -rn "async def build_help_menu_view" disbot/cogs --include=*.py | wc -l` → 43.
- `grep -rn "_resolve_projection" disbot/ --include=*.py` → 6 call sites (navigation.py:325; help_cog.py:175,267,287,393; panels.py:104).
- `grep -rn "role_feasibility" disbot/ --include=*.py | grep -v "utils/role_feasibility.py"` → 28 refs across 13 modules.
- `grep -rn "HubChildButton" ...` → 3 subclasses (community, games, utility).
- `grep -cn '"setup"' disbot/utils/subsystem_registry.py` → 0.
- python/regex parse of subsystem_registry.py blocks → 43 subsystems; visibility_tier Counter({'user': 26, 'administrator': 15, 'moderator': 1, 'staff': 1}); parent_hub Counter({'games': 10, 'community': 7, 'admin': 6, 'moderation': 6, 'economy': 3, 'utility': 2}).
- python/ast over disbot/cogs for prefix `@commands.command`/`@commands.group` → 243 total, 90 carrying an operator-gate decorator.
- python/ast over essential_setup.py step classes → 8 steps, 13 build_items/refresh_items bodies.
- `grep -rn "views.setup" disbot/ --include=*.py | grep -v "^disbot/views/setup/\|^disbot/cogs/setup"` → the only opener outside the setup package is cogs/quicksetup_cog.py.
- `grep -rn "AutomodCog\|SecurityCog\|ProofChannel\|ImageModeration" disbot/views disbot/cogs --include=*.py` (excluding their own cogs) → no output.

JOURNEY TRACES (interaction = one Discord component/modal submit; typed = a prefix/slash command the user must type).

(a) New server owner runs setup. Automatic: setup_cog.py:604-606 on_guild_join → _handle_join (613-641) → private #superbot-setup, else post_launcher (launcher.py:540-596) picks the safest existing channel, else DMs the owner. Then 1 interaction (Start Setup, launcher.py:192-248) → Essential Setup posted in the setup channel + an ephemeral jump link. Flow = 8 steps (essential_setup.py:70-79); every step carries Skip (163-178). Minimum 8 more interactions (skip everything) to reach the summary; ≥20 to configure all eight (counted per-step items: 2+3+2+2+2+≥3+3+3). Typed command required: NO if the launcher message still exists; YES (`!setup`/`/setup`) otherwise — nothing in the Help/hub click graph opens setup (see P2-D3).

(b) Member self-assigns a role. Only member-facing path is a already-posted RoleMenuView: 1 interaction (button role_menu_view.py:153-179 or select 181-210) → ephemeral confirmation. 0 typed. Not reachable through Help: subsystem_registry "role" is `"visibility_tier": "administrator"`, so it is neither a Community child button nor a routable `!help roles` for a member. Operator prerequisite to publish the menu: `!roles` (typed) → 💬 Reaction Roles → 🛠️ Role Menus → ➕ New Menu → 🏷️ Roles → pick roles → 📍 Channel → pick channel → 🚀 Post = 8 interactions + 1 typed.

(c) Operator changes a setting. `!settings` (typed, admin_or_owner, settings_cog.py:120-143) OR Help home → Server & Admin (1) → 🛠 Settings (2). Then subsystem select (3) → "Edit a setting…" select (4); a bool writes immediately (edit_boolean.py:57-88), an enum/number/text needs one more widget interaction (5). So 4–5 interactions from Help home, and reaching Help home itself needs a typed `!help`/`/help` unless the operator is already on a panel carrying 📚 Help.

(d) Member opens a ticket. Public launcher panel: click (1) → modal submit (2) = 2 interactions, 0 typed. Via Help: `!help` (typed) → Community (1) → Support Tickets (2) → Open a ticket (3) → modal submit (4) = 4 interactions + 1 typed. Eligibility is one seam (ticket_service.py:109-135) with per-reason copy (69-85).

(e) Operator recovers from a lockout. command_access.py:41-68 lists 24 bootstrap names (help, setup, settings, admin, adminmenu, diag, platform, …); :351-360 admits them for guild owner/administrator/manage_guild regardless of the guild's stored policy; the denial copy (:243-253) names `!setup` and `!settings` verbatim. Recovery = 1 typed + 2 interactions (`!settings` → 🚪 Command access → All channels, settings/hub.py:300-327 + edit_command_access.py:252-265), or 1 typed + 9 interactions via `!setup` (7 skips then step 8, essential_setup.py:1917-1943). A typed command is REQUIRED — there is no button path into recovery.

(3) DEGRADED STATES, cited: governance-hidden → the entry is simply absent from Home/hub, and a typed name renders the same not-found embed as a typo (route.py:19-26, 279-280, 304-305) — deliberate no-leak, but it makes "hidden" and "misspelt" indistinguishable. Click-time recheck on hub children → "That feature is no longer available in this channel." (hub_children.py:163-170). Feature-flag kill switch → an explicit disabled embed naming the flag and the env override (settings_cog.py:49-78). Cog crashed at boot → subsystem marked INTERNAL and hidden (bot1.py:740-754 + resolver.py:294-305). Missing Manage Channels → setup falls back to the invoking channel with a hint (essential_setup.py:2424-2427) on the typed path but hard-stops on the launcher button (launcher.py:229-236). Role above the bot → blocked up front in the builder (role_menu_builder.py:709-715), silently dropped on partial success at click time (reaction_role_service.py:778-781). Ticket channel creation refused → member-facing ephemeral naming a permission the member cannot grant (ticket_mutation.py:145-152). Missing gateway INTENT → nothing: intents are hardcoded at bot1.py:76-78 and a repo-wide grep for privileged-intent handling found no runtime path.

(4) ONE GRAPH OR TWO: one member graph, registry-driven and governance-filtered, plus a second hand-rolled operator graph. Both enter through the same HelpCategoryView and the same _resolve_projection (6 call sites), so tier filtering is one decision — but only 3 of 8 hubs (games, community, utility) build their children through the shared HubChildButton/discover_hub_children seam; admin, moderation, economy, btd6 and project_moon hand-write theirs. The Server & Admin panel carries 9 hand-written navigation buttons keyed by cog CLASS-NAME STRINGS with no click-time governance recheck (admin_cog.py:729-778), against 6 registry primary_children — and 2 of those 9 (Logging, Cleanup) are declared children of the moderation hub, while 1 (Platform) is not a subsystem at all.

strengths.claim: Every Help render path builds its audience view through one seam: _resolve_projection is called at exactly 6 sites (counted) — !help, /help, the Home dropdown callback, the back-to-Help builder, resolve_help_panel_state, and the universal 📚 Help button in views/navigation.py — so Home, the typed route, the dropdown and every Back button cannot disagree about what a given member can see.
strengths.quote:
async def _resolve_projection(gctx: GovernanceContext) -> HelpProjection:
    """Governance + guild Help overlay → the audience projection (HLP-2/3).

    The cog's one projection-construction seam: every entry point and
    click-time re-check builds its :class:`HelpProjection` here, so the
    governance resolve (mockable via ``governance_service``) and the
    HLP-3 overlay fetch (cached; empty for DMs/faults) can never diverge
    across render paths.
    """
    vis_result = await governance_service.resolve_visibility(gctx)
    overlay = await help_overlay.get_guild_help_overlay(gctx.guild_id or None)
    return HelpProjection.from_visibility(vis_result, overlay=overlay)
strengths.prevents_failure: Help surfaces disagreeing about what exists for one member — a hub visible on Home that the dropdown refuses to open, or a Back button returning to a menu built from a stale tier snapshot
strengths.successor_recommendation: Keep exactly one async projection constructor and make every entry point (typed, slash, component, back-builder) call it; do not let a panel builder resolve governance itself.

strengths.claim: The 'never stranded' contract is a constructor-level auto-attach with a CI gate behind it: attach_standard_nav runs from exactly 2 base-class __init__s (views/base.py:168-170, core/runtime/persistent_views.py:110-112), 53 panel classes declare a SUBSYSTEM (counted; an ast cross-check found 0 values unknown to the registry), and scripts/check_consistency.py ships rule 'back_button' at severity="error" which .github/workflows/code-quality.yml:211 runs as `--mode strict`.
strengths.quote:
def attach_standard_nav(view: discord.ui.View) -> None:
    """Auto-attach the universal Help (+ Back-to-hub) controls to a panel.

    The "never stranded" mechanism (owner directive 2026-06-23): every panel
    that declares a ``SUBSYSTEM`` gets, on construction, a **📚 Help** button
    (opens the Help home) and — when the subsystem has a ``parent_hub`` — a
    **↩ <hub>** button (rebuilds its mother hub). Because this runs in the base
    view ``__init__``, the controls reappear on every redraw onto a fresh view
    instance (the ``edit_in_place`` idiom that previously dropped them), and any
    panel reachable by *any* command stays one click from Help and its hub.
strengths.prevents_failure: a leaf panel opened by any command has no way back to Help or its hub, and loses whatever back button a parent pushed the first time the panel redraws onto a fresh view instance
strengths.successor_recommendation: Put nav attachment in the base view constructor (not in each panel, not pushed by parents), and keep a linter that fails the build on a navigable panel with no parent affordance. Do not reproduce the label-substring heuristic in _self_navigates — key the opt-out off an explicit class flag.

strengths.claim: Lockout recovery is a closed loop enforced in the single admission resolver: a 24-name bootstrap allowlist bypasses the guild's own command-access policy for owner/administrator/manage_guild on both surfaces (2 consumers: the prefix _channel_guard and the slash tree interaction_check, both installed by the cog config.INITIAL_EXTENSIONS[0] pins first), the denial copy names `!setup` and `!settings` verbatim, and Essential Setup step 8 is the thing that can set and unset the lockout.
strengths.prevents_failure: an operator sets command access to disabled_except_bootstrap (or a channel allowlist that excludes every channel they use) and can never re-open the bot, because every command that could undo it is itself denied
strengths.successor_recommendation: Keep an explicit always-admitted operator command set, keep denial copy that names the recovery command, and make the setting that causes the lockout live in the same flow that can undo it. tests/unit/runtime/test_command_access_resolver.py:319-353 asserts the allowed/reason effect under disabled_except_bootstrap — carry that test shape over.

strengths.claim: A cog that fails to load is removed from the navigation graph rather than left as a dead category: _load_cogs marks every subsystem whose entry_point commands are absent, and the visibility resolver turns those into SubsystemState.INTERNAL, which is excluded from visible_subsystems and therefore from Home, from every hub child list, and from the typed route.
strengths.prevents_failure: a member clicks a Help category whose cog crashed at boot and lands on an erroring or empty panel with no explanation
strengths.successor_recommendation: Wire load failures into the same visibility state machine the UI already consults, so a broken feature disappears from navigation instead of being discovered by clicking it. Note the gap this does NOT cover: a cog that loads but whose panel builder raises at click time still renders the not-found embed (see P2-D2 family).

strengths.claim: First contact has a three-tier delivery ladder so the owner always gets the setup entry point: private #superbot-setup channel → the safest existing channel → owner DM. post_launcher has 2 consumers (setup_cog.py:627 on join, launcher.py:436 the Repost button) and _handle_join calls it as the fallback when the private-channel path returns (None, None).
strengths.prevents_failure: the bot joins a server, cannot create or post in its setup channel, and nobody ever learns setup exists — the silent-install failure
strengths.successor_recommendation: Keep the ladder, but see P2-D5: the button the ladder delivers must degrade the same way the typed command does, and the DM rung must produce a panel whose buttons actually work outside a guild.

strengths.claim: Setup is direct-apply plus restart-revivable: each step writes through its audited service immediately, only the UI position is persisted after every navigation move, and an interrupted flow is bridged by a persistent one-button resume view swept in on on_ready (setup_cog.py:608-611 calls revive_essential_flows).
strengths.quote:
async def persist_progress(self) -> None:
        """Persist the flow position so a restart can revive it (migration 099).

        Called after every navigation move.  Best-effort: a DB hiccup must
        never break the wizard.  When the flow reaches the summary it is
        finished — clear the anchor and mark the session complete so the
        launcher reflects it and the on-ready resume sweep stops trying to
        revive a done flow.  Essential Setup is direct-apply, so only the *UI
        position* is stored here; the configuration is already saved.
        """
strengths.prevents_failure: a bot restart mid-setup leaves the operator with a dead message and loses every choice they had made — the staged-draft-lost-on-deploy class
strengths.simpler_than_counterpart: The advanced wizard's staged draft → Final Review path needs a session row and cross-restart anchor persistence; Essential Setup needs only an integer step index because nothing is staged.
strengths.successor_recommendation: Make onboarding direct-apply by default so a crash costs a message, not a configuration; persist only the cursor, and re-render from live state.

strengths.claim: 'Can the bot actually manage this role?' is one pure, reason-coded seam (utils/role_feasibility.py) consumed by 13 modules and 28 call sites (counted), and the self-role builder uses it to refuse up front with an actionable instruction instead of letting the operator publish a menu that will silently no-op.
strengths.prevents_failure: an operator publishes a public self-role menu built from roles the bot cannot grant, and every member click silently does nothing
strengths.successor_recommendation: Keep one pure feasibility evaluator with reason codes and short labels, used by pickers, services and diagnostics alike — and fix the reporting half (P2-D4): the seam already knows which ids were blocked, the UI just does not say so on partial success.

strengths.claim: The shared hub→child button re-resolves governance at click time and fails closed with plain copy, so a panel that has been sitting in a channel cannot open a subsystem that was disabled since it rendered. Three hubs (community, games, utility) bind this one button class as thin subclasses (counted: 3 HubChildButton subclasses, 3 discover_hub_children call sites).
strengths.quote:
async def callback(self, interaction: discord.Interaction) -> None:
        # Click-time governance recheck: a child that became invisible since
        # render fails closed with an ephemeral (resolve is cached → ~free).
        gctx = GovernanceContext.from_interaction(interaction)
        vis_result = await governance_service.resolve_visibility(gctx)
        if self._subsystem not in vis_result.visible_subsystems:
            await interaction.response.send_message(
                "That feature is no longer available in this channel.",
                ephemeral=True,
            )
            return
strengths.prevents_failure: a stale rendered panel lets a member open a subsystem an operator disabled after the panel was drawn — render-time visibility outliving the policy that produced it
strengths.successor_recommendation: Have exactly ONE child-forwarding button class with the recheck baked in and make every hub — operator hubs included — use it; superbot only got 3 of 8 hubs onto it (see P2-D8).

defects.claim: The Moderation & Safety hub panel renders none of the 6 children the hub registry declares for it. hub_registry.py:174-181 lists automod, image_moderation, cleanup, logging, proof_channel, security as primary_children; moderation_cog.build_help_menu_view returns ModPanelView, whose entire class body (views/moderation/main_panel.py, 128 lines total) is 7 action buttons — Warn, Timeout, Kick, Ban, Unban, Mod Logs, Clear Warnings — and no child navigation. A repo-wide grep for AutomodCog/SecurityCog/ProofChannel/ImageModeration outside their own cog files returned no output: nothing anywhere opens those four panels except their own typed commands.
defects.quote:
HubEntry(
        key="moderation",
        display_name="Moderation & Safety",
        emoji="🛡️",
        purpose="Warnings, timeouts, bans, cleanup, audit logs.",
        entry_command="!modmenu",
        primary_children=(
            "automod",
            "image_moderation",
            "cleanup",
            "logging",
            "proof_channel",
            "security",
        ),
defects.failure_scenario: A server administrator wants to turn on spam and bad-link protection. They type !help, pick 🛡️ Moderation & Safety from the dropdown — a category whose own one-line purpose says "Warnings, timeouts, bans, cleanup, audit logs" — and get a panel with Warn / Timeout / Kick / Ban / Unban / Mod Logs / Clear Warnings. There is no Automod button, no Security button, no Cleanup button and no Logging button on that panel or anywhere reachable from it, so the click journey dead-ends. The only way through is to already know the literal string !automod (or !security / !imagemod / !cleanup / !logging / !prizemenu).
defects.successor_recommendation: A hub's children must be rendered from the same registry field that declares them — one shared child-button class, no hub allowed to hand-roll its own list. If a hub panel wants action buttons too, they live alongside the discovered children, not instead of them.

defects.claim: The reachability invariant that CI runs proves reachability in a REGISTRY MODEL, not in the rendered panel, which is exactly why P2-D1 ships green. scheme_live() builds each section's children by filtering SUBSYSTEMS on parent_hub and never looks at what the hub's build_help_menu_view actually returns; check_reachability then counts clicks in that model.
defects.quote:
def scheme_live() -> Scheme:
    """The live registry exactly: hubs + their primary_children (via the
    parent_hub filter); everything else would fall to the Advanced browser.

    After PR #1290 this reads the consolidated grouping straight from the
    registry, so the sim doubles as a regression check: if a future edit
    re-orphans a subsystem or re-crowds the index, the numbers move here.
    """
    from utils.hub_registry import HUBS

    sections = []
    for hub in HUBS:
        children = [k for k, v in LEAVES.items() if v.get("parent_hub") == hub.key]
        children.sort(key=lambda k: LEAVES[k].get("ui_priority", 999))
        sections.append(Section(hub.key, hub.display_name, children))
    return Scheme("live", sections)
defects.failure_scenario: A maintainer adds a subsystem, sets parent_hub="moderation", and ships. tests/unit/invariants/test_help_reachability.py passes (the sim sees it homed under a hub within MAX_CLICKS) and .github/workflows/code-quality.yml goes green, while the running Moderation panel — 7 hardcoded buttons — renders no button for it. The team believes navigation reachability is CI-enforced; six subsystems are already click-unreachable behind that green check.
defects.successor_recommendation: Assert reachability against the components a panel actually produces (construct the view and read view.children / custom_ids), not against a hand-written model of the registry. A guard that simulates the UI instead of instantiating it will always drift from the UI.

defects.claim: The single most important operator journey — first-time setup — sits outside both the click graph and every reachability guard. `"setup"` appears 0 times as a key in disbot/utils/subsystem_registry.py (grep -c → 0), so it is neither a hub nor a hub child and the Help dropdown (which lists hubs only) can never reach it. The Server & Admin panel has 13 buttons (admin_cog.py:512-717) and none of them is Setup. And the per-command reachability checker exempts it by construction: !setup carries @admin_or_owner() (quicksetup_cog.py:33), and _classify returns "exempt" for tier operator/owner — 90 of the 243 prefix commands/groups in disbot/cogs carry such a decorator (ast count).
defects.failure_scenario: A server owner dismisses the on-join launcher (or the channel it landed in gets cleaned up, or they invited the bot months ago). Later they want to configure it. They type !help, open the only operator category — ⚙️ Server & Admin — and see Server Stats, Cog List, Reload All, Log Level, Settings, Server Management, Channels, AI, Platform, Diagnostics, UX Lab, Logging, Cleanup, Help. No Setup. No button anywhere in the graph opens the wizard: a grep for imports of views.setup outside the setup package finds only cogs/quicksetup_cog.py. They must already know the literal string `!setup`, and no CI guard would ever have flagged that, because operator commands are exempt from the only per-command reachability ratchet.
defects.successor_recommendation: Setup is a first-class destination: register it in the same registry the navigation graph is built from, give it a button on the operator hub, and make the reachability guard cover operator journeys instead of exempting the entire operator surface.

defects.claim: A partially-failed self-role pick is reported to the member as a complete success. _apply only sets the explanatory note when NOTHING succeeded (`if blocked and not (added or removed)`), and the UI formatter renders only added / removed / note — `outcome.blocked` is never shown.
defects.failure_scenario: A member opens a multi-select role menu and picks three roles — Gamer, Artist, and Verified. Verified sits above the bot's highest role (or someone moved the bot down since the menu was published). apply_selection adds two, blocks one, and because added is non-empty the note stays empty; role_menu_view._format_outcome (lines 412-431) builds its reply from added/removed/note only, so the ephemeral reads "✅ Added **Gamer**, **Artist**" with no mention of Verified. The member believes they hold Verified, does not get access to the gated channel, and the operator has no signal that the menu is half-broken.
defects.successor_recommendation: Any partial-effect outcome must render all three lists — succeeded, refused, and why. The blocked ids and their reason codes are already computed by role_feasibility; the bug is purely that the confirmation drops them when anything else succeeded.

defects.claim: The on-join launcher's Start Setup button and the !setup command call the same function and degrade differently: the button hard-stops on reason == "no_channel", while open_essential_setup_prefix/open_essential_setup fall back to opening the flow inline in the invoking channel with an explanatory hint.
defects.quote:
channel, message, reason = await open_essential_setup_in_setup_channel(
            guild,
            member,
        )
        if reason == "no_channel" or channel is None:
            await interaction.response.send_message(
                "I couldn't ensure the private `#superbot-setup` channel — "
                "I need the **Manage Channels** permission.  Grant it and "
                "try again.",
                ephemeral=True,
            )
            return
defects.failure_scenario: An owner invites the bot with a conservative role that lacks Manage Channels. _handle_join cannot create #superbot-setup, so post_launcher drops the launcher into #general instead. The owner clicks the big green Start Setup button — the only affordance the bot has given them — and is told to go grant a permission and try again. Typing `!setup` in that same channel would instead have opened the whole eight-step flow inline with the hint at essential_setup.py:2424-2427 ("so I've opened setup right here instead"). The button, which is the first-run surface, is strictly worse than the command it wraps, at exactly the moment permissions are most likely to be under-granted.
defects.successor_recommendation: One entry function per journey, with the degradation ladder inside it — never a button that reimplements the command's error handling less generously. The same rule catches the DM rung: every button on SetupLauncherView gates on isinstance(member, discord.Member), so an owner-DM'd launcher (launcher.py:572-582) delivers a panel whose Start Setup answers "This can only be used in a server."

defects.claim: The terminal screen of the explicitly button-only, 'zero jargon' setup flow is a list of seven commands to type. _EXTRAS (essential_setup.py:1980-2023) holds 7 entries and build_extras_embed renders each as an embed field ending "Open with `!command`" — !starboard, !counters, !security, !imagemod, !karma, !aimenu, !reactroles — with no button for any of them.
defects.quote:
def build_extras_embed() -> discord.Embed:
    """Render the one-screen extras menu (kept here so its copy stays plain)."""
    embed = discord.Embed(
        title="✨ More you can set up",
        description=(
            "These are all optional — turn on any that fit your server. "
            "Run the command shown under each one to set it up."
        ),
        color=discord.Color.blurple(),
    )
    for extra in _EXTRAS:
        embed.add_field(
            name=f"{extra.emoji} {extra.label}",
            value=f"{extra.blurb}\nOpen with `{extra.command}`",
            inline=False,
        )
    return embed
defects.failure_scenario: An owner completes all eight setup steps without typing anything — the module docstring promises a flow that "needs **zero Discord/bot knowledge**, uses **no jargon**" and is "button/dropdown-only". On the summary screen they press ✨ More to set up and are handed seven fields each saying "Open with `!starboard`" etc. To turn on reaction roles they must now leave the flow, remember the prefix, and type a command — the exact skill the flow was built to avoid requiring. Four of the seven (!security, !imagemod, !reactroles, !counters) have no button path anywhere else either.
defects.successor_recommendation: If the extras are worth listing on the completion screen they are worth a button that opens the target panel in place; a completion screen that hands out commands is the discoverability failure the flow exists to fix, restated at the end of it.

defects.claim: !roles carries no permission decorator, is not hidden, and opens an operator-only panel to any member: 6 of the 7 buttons on RoleHubPanelView re-check manage_roles or administrator and deny (role_cog.py:97-266), and the hub embed advertises all seven with no indication that any of them is restricted.
defects.quote:
@commands.command(name="roles")
    async def roles_hub(self, ctx: commands.Context) -> None:
        """Open the role management hub."""
        view = RoleHubPanelView()
        embed = _build_role_hub_embed()
        msg = await panel_manager.get_or_render_panel(ctx, "role", embed, view)
        view.message = msg
defects.failure_scenario: A member wants to pick a role, types !roles (an obvious guess; the command is not hidden and command_access defaults to all_channels). They get a 🎭 Role Hub embed listing Create / Manage / Time Roles / XP Roles / Reaction Roles / Diagnostics / Exemptions with a one-line description each and no permission marker. Pressing Create or Manage returns "❌ You need **Manage Roles** permission."; Time Roles, XP Roles, Diagnostics and Exemptions return "❌ You need **Administrator** permission."; the seventh, Reaction Roles, opens a panel where every action re-checks manage_roles and denies. Six of seven buttons are dead on contact and the panel never says so. Meanwhile the actual member-facing self-assign surface — a posted role menu — is unreachable from Help at all, because the "role" subsystem is visibility_tier "administrator".
defects.successor_recommendation: Render only the controls the viewer can use (the projection machinery already resolves the tier — the hub embed just does not consult it), and give members their own self-assign entry rather than routing them into the operator panel. Deny-on-click is the last line, not the design.

defects.claim: There are two navigation implementations, and the operator one is the weaker: 3 of 8 hubs use the shared registry-driven HubChildButton (with its click-time governance recheck), while the Server & Admin panel hand-writes 9 navigation buttons resolved by cog CLASS-NAME STRING through interaction.client.get_cog, with no governance recheck. Its button set also diverges from the registry: hub_registry declares 6 admin primary_children, the panel offers 9 destinations, 2 of which (Logging, Cleanup) are declared children of the moderation hub and 1 of which (Platform) is not a subsystem at all.

defects.failure_scenario: An operator turns Logging off for the server through a governance visibility override. In the member-side graph that works: the hub child button re-resolves visibility on click and answers "That feature is no longer available in this channel." On the operator side it does not: Help → ⚙️ Server & Admin → 📝 Logging goes through _open_via_help_hook, which resolves LoggingCog by class-name string and calls build_help_menu_view with no visibility check, so the full Logging panel opens anyway. Separately, a rename of any of the eight literal cog names ("SettingsCog", "ServerManagementCog", "ChannelCog", "AICog", "DiagnosticCog", "LoggingCog", "UX Lab", "Cleanup") turns that button into an orange "<name> unavailable" embed with nothing pinning the strings — a grep of tests/ for _open_via_help_hook or those cog_name= arguments returns no test covering this call site.
defects.successor_recommendation: One navigation implementation for both audiences: children discovered from the registry, resolved by a stable key rather than a class-name string, and re-checked against policy at click time. Operator surfaces need the recheck more than member surfaces, not less.

honest_nulls: Nothing here was exercised against a live bot or a live guild. discord.py is not installed in this container (`import discord` → ModuleNotFoundError), so scripts/check_command_reachability.py could not be run and no view could be instantiated. Every interaction count is a static trace of button/select/modal definitions and their callbacks, not an observed click path; a runtime branch I did not read could add or remove a step.

I could not establish what the Help dropdown actually renders for a specific member tier, because visible_hubs() depends on a live governance resolve against a guild's scope-chain overrides. The tier arithmetic is stated from the registry (43 subsystems: 26 user, 15 administrator, 1 moderator, 1 staff; 8 hubs, 2 of them above user tier) plus _hub_decision's ordering; a guild-level override could hide or expose more.

I could not verify whether component (button) interactions bypass the command-access gate. BootstrapAccessCog installs bot.tree.interaction_check, which in discord.py governs app commands; component interactions are dispatched through the view store. If that reading is right, every already-posted panel keeps working under disabled_except_bootstrap — a real behaviour with policy implications — but I did not have the library available to confirm the dispatch path, and superbot's own source does not state it.

No intent-degradation handling exists to cite, and I could not establish what the operator sees if a privileged intent is off. bot1.py:76-78 sets `intents.message_content = True` / `intents.members = True` unconditionally, and a repo-wide grep for privileged-intent handling returned only unrelated uses of the word 'intent' (BTD6 query resolution, notification intents). Whether a PrivilegedIntentsRequired login failure is surfaced anywhere is unknown from source alone.

The _self_navigates heuristic (views/navigation.py:368-404) skips the universal nav attach whenever any child's label contains 'help' or 'back to', and the code itself says 'Heuristic — if a future panel's button copy diverges this may misfire'. I looked for a SUBSYSTEM-declaring panel whose only back-token control is a lateral or self-refresh and did not find a confirmed stranded case (the deathmatch/RPS sub-views carry a real back to their own parent panel, which itself has Help). I am recording this as an unproven risk, not a defect.

I did not establish how many of the 43 subsystems' build_help_menu_view hooks actually succeed. 43 cogs define the hook (counted) and 43 subsystems exist, but the mapping is not 1:1 (creature_battle_cog defines a hook and is not a registry key; help_cog defines none). Confirming per-subsystem hook coverage needs the live _cog_for_subsystem entry_points match, which requires a running bot.

The claim that P2-D1's six moderation children are click-unreachable is scoped to what I searched: the Help dropdown (hubs only), hub child buttons (moderation renders none), the Admin panel (Logging and Cleanup only, administrator-tier), and cross-references to their cog classes (grep returned nothing). A hand-wired button inside some panel I did not open could still reach one of them; I read every file that names those cogs and found none.

Ticket-permission failure surfacing is a smaller finding I verified but did not file as a defect row: ticket_mutation.py:145-152 returns 'I couldn't create the ticket channel — I may be missing the **Manage Channels** permission.' to the member who clicked, via _shared.py:105, with no staff notification anywhere in open_ticket. The member is shown a permission they cannot grant. I left it out only because the row budget was full, not because it is refuted.
